# Adjacency from a pair list

**Claim.** In the simple graph generated by a list of ordered pairs, $u$ and $v$ are adjacent exactly when one of $(u,v)$ and $(v,u)$ occurs in the list and $u\ne v$.

**Proof.** By the definition of the graph generated from an edge set, adjacency means that some listed pair gives the same unordered edge as $\{u,v\}$, with $u\ne v$. Equality of unordered pairs has two possibilities: the listed pair is $(u,v)$, or it is $(v,u)$. Conversely, either occurrence gives the corresponding unordered edge, and together with $u\ne v$ this is precisely adjacency.
